description: Dependency doctrine (2026-07-14): pin versions (rangeStrategy pin), pin the behaviors we rely on with tests, then bump as eagerly as possible — behind GREEN CI, so we are always first to know when something breaks. automerge waits for tests by DEFAULT: there is deliberately NO global ignoreTests (it previously merged BEFORE CI, inverting the doctrine — breakage landed on main instead of being caught in the PR). The one exception to eagerness is npm supply chain (see the npm rule): tests cannot catch a malicious publish, so time is the guard.

packageRules.description: npm supply chain is a DIFFERENT threat model: tests catch breakage, not a malicious/compromised publish (it passes every test and still backdoors). Time is the only defense — a bad release is typically yanked within days. Hold every npm update 7 days before it is eligible to automerge. The deliberate exception to eager bumping.

The age hold is npm-ONLY (see the npm rule). GitHub-Actions/Docker pins are supply-chain HARDENING — pinning a floating @v6 to an exact version/digest is the safe direction, not a freshness-chasing bump — so an age gate does them no good and actively harms: PR #20 bundled ~20 actions into one rolling `pin dependencies` batch whose age window reset every time ANY of the 20 released, so it never aged and sat open 10 days. Zero the hold explicitly for these datasources so a green-CI action/docker pin or bump automerges immediately.
solaris vmactions confs mix toolchain variants (gcc/clang) into one namespace; track only the gcc line the leg is built around.

THE TOOLCHAIN NODE IS ONE DEPENDENCY PINNED IN THREE PLACES, and Renovate sees three: .tool-versions (asdf), ci.yml's oracle `container: image: node:<v>-alpine`, and docker-loop/Dockerfile.xfuse's `FROM node:<v>-bookworm-slim`. ci.yml's own guard requires the container's node to EQUAL .tool-versions exactly, so any split takes both node-shim-oracle jobs down. Group them so one PR moves all three, and gate the same invariant in test/node-pins-agree.test.cjs, because a hand-edit or a partially-merged PR can still split what this groups. AND THE BINDING CONSTRAINT IS DOCKER HUB, NOT nodejs.org: on 2026-08-27 a bump to 24.20.0 landed in .tool-versions while Docker Hub's newest was node:24.19.0-alpine, and 'matching' the container to it failed as `manifest unknown` before the job ran a line of our code. Publishing is not simultaneous. So allowedVersions holds this group to what an image actually exists for; the toolchain pin follows image availability rather than dragging it. package.json engines.node is EXCLUDED deliberately: that is the node a built naude EMBEDS, on its own major.
packageRules.groupName: node toolchain (asdf + oracle container + xfuse image)
